part_1_vacuous_green_control.why_neither_run_can_be_green_without_lat: The counter grades only events ancestral to the round it is labelled with, and it scores an event only through a committed late-register row whose OWN introducing commit is a strict descendant of the event commit. With --round 82 at the base it cannot even evaluate: the frozen plan it reads the base from does not exist at aaf974db (exit 2). With --round 81 it is green (late=10) precisely because the ten round-81 late rows are committed in that tree; that population contains none of the five round-81 record-edit events (cf28c470, 37484391, 50c711ec, 93cdfd60, 017c34ca) whose 15 undeclared lines are the round-82 debt, and the base register has 88 rows with zero rows for those events. Delete the late rows and the same run goes red: a header-only register turns the ten events they accepted into unaccepted=10 with 88 count-short findings. Pass rows through --late instead of the committed register and they are unbound-register (late_intro=None, no per-row blame), so they accept nothing. A register-free or out-of-band run therefore cannot print the green line; at the base the --round 82 line is not merely red but unevaluable, because the elements are per-event committed rows with resolvable introductions, not a counter that wiring can satisfy.
